# members of `coll` rendered as text with `sep` between them.
# WHY IT EXISTS. A spread can put a separator AFTER each element;
# putting one BETWEEN N elements is a reduction over strings, and the
# language had none -- `sum` is numeric, `+` does not reduce a list, and
# indexed concatenation needs the arity known in advance. So a generated

# exact digits of a big integer. The renderer is literally shared
# ORDER is source order for a list and cmpCodePoint-sorted key order for

# A pref separator contributes its preferred value, as a pref member does.
# THE STAGING RULE (G8 phase 0): a fold over a bag still being merged
# into folds the wrong bag, so the call waits for the model to settle.
# It canons as its call, reparses to itself, and hashes identically in
# both ports -- the same contract every unfired generator keeps.
# This is the half of the design that is not obvious, and getting it
# wrong in either direction is the defect that matters.
# An UNSETTLED member -- an unresolved kind, a top, a preferred
# disjunct that has not collapsed -- is NOT a join failure. The call
# stays residual and generation reports it as ordinary incompleteness
# requires. Refusing these would make `join` unusable inside a schema.
# NOTE the class difference from `sum`, which answers `invalid-arg`
# (conflict) for this same shape. Both ports agree here, so it is not a
# parity break; it is `join` calling an uncollapsed disjunction
# UNFINISHED where `sum` calls it WRONG. `join`'s reading is the one
# this design argues for -- the value is not yet a value.
# A SETTLED non-text member is `join_member`, class conflict, and it is
# refused HERE rather than at generation. `+` with a string on the left
# RESIDUATES on a map or a null rather than refusing, so folding blindly
# would report the failure late, naming the whole call instead of the
# A refusal inside the fold IS the answer, as it is for `sum`: folding
# on past it would report the wrong reason, or none.
# ---- the separator is a STRING or it is nothing ----
# A number would render perfectly well through `+` and is still refused:
# the separator is not a member of the fold, it is the parameter naming
# the text between members, and `join(x, 5)` is far likelier a mistake.
